rose.description: A classic flowering shrub known for its layered, fragrant petals. Roses come in hundreds of cultivated varieties and colors, and have been cultivated for thousands of years.

sunflower.description: A tall, fast-growing plant with a large flower head of golden petals surrounding a dense center of seeds. Known for heliotropism — young flowers track the sun across the sky.

daffodil.description: A trumpet-shaped spring bulb flower, usually yellow or white, often among the first blooms to appear after winter.

tiger lily.description: A bold orange lily with distinctive black spots on its petals, native to eastern Asia. Its bulbs are edible and used in some Asian cuisines.

petunia.description: A popular garden and container flower with trumpet-shaped blooms in a wide range of colors, valued for blooming continuously through summer.

hibiscus.description: A large, showy tropical flower with five broad petals and a prominent central stamen, often used in teas and as a national/state flower symbol.

water lily.description: An aquatic flower that floats on still water, with broad round leaves (lily pads) and star-shaped blooms that open in the morning and close at night.

magnolia.description: An ancient flowering plant genus with large, waxy, fragrant blooms, predating bees — originally pollinated by beetles.

carnation.description: A ruffled, long-lasting cut flower available in many colors, commonly used in bouquets and boutonnieres.

foxglove.description: A tall spike of tubular, bell-shaped flowers, typically purple or white with speckled throats. Note: the plant is toxic if ingested.
